subject: Ava Retail throughput shape + SLO clarifications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@avaretail.com>, Gabe Turner <gabe.turner@avaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Ava Retail discovery — throughput shape & SLO asks

Thanks again for the 30m earlier, Priya and Gabe — great context on sessionized checkout flows and the 2-step recommendation generator. Quick recap + the asks we discussed so we can size reliably:

- Primary latency target: 99th <= 300ms for single-turn recommend calls (we'll confirm with perf team).
- Typical session: 3–6 requests (interactive), many are short prompts (~120 tokens); a small subset (cart summarization) is ~1,200 tokens.
- Traffic shape you called out: baseline ~12 QPS steady (mostly daytime), with two daily peaks ~120 QPS for 30–45s during flash sales.
- Streaming: you want partial token streaming for the recommendation pipeline for the interactive UI.

As next steps, please send a 24–72h sample of real traffic (timestamps + token counts + sample prompt lengths) — we flagged two ways to share below. I attached our SLO/throughput template to make it quick (redwood_slo_template.xlsx).

We also want to confirm: is the flash-sale peak predictable (cron-driven) or user-driven? That affects burst provisioning and autoscale windows.

Attachments: [Attachment: avaretail_traffic_sample.tsv (text/tsv)] [Attachment: redwood_slo_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks — I'll loop in Marissa for the sizing sketch once we have the sample.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Ava Retail discovery — throughput shape & SLO asks

Karthik — thanks for the recap and the template. Quick answers inline:

- Flash-sales are a mix: some are scheduled (we run a daily 11:00am PST drop), others are promoted by marketing and can be ad-hoc. Expect both patterns.
- I've attached a 48h anonymized extract (avaretail_traffic_sample.tsv) with timestamps, token counts, and a flag for streaming vs non-streaming. The 120 QPS crest you noted is representative of the biggest sale window; most crest windows are 20–90s long.
- We want streaming for the interactive recommender (low-latency partial results) and non-streaming for the batch summarization endpoint.

Two asks from our side: can you provide a rough cost / GPU sizing estimate for (a) steady-state + autoscale and (b) a plan for handling two concurrent crest windows? Also procurement will want language around data retention and audit logs — Gabe, looping you in.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@avaretail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Ava Retail discovery — throughput shape & SLO asks

Thanks for the sample, Priya — this is super helpful. I pulled a quick summary and a sketch for capacity planning. High-level observations from the TSV:

- 48h sample shows baseline ~10–15 QPS (matches your note) with median prompt length ~110 tokens and 97th ~860 tokens because of longer summaries.
- Crest windows in the sample: two major crest spikes (peak ~115–130 QPS) lasting 25s and 52s; a handful of smaller spikes to ~50 QPS lasting <20s.
- Streaming endpoints are ~40% of interactive requests and have stricter tail latency expectations.

Sizing sketch (very rough):
- Steady: 2 x small inference pools (8xA10-like GPU equiv) with autoscale headroom for 2x baseline during marketing bursts.
- Crest handling: recommend warm standby capacity and short autoscale cooldowns; two concurrent crest windows of ~120 QPS each will require either: 1) burst capacity (policy-based) or 2) pre-warmed dedicated capacity sized to the expected combined crest (~240 QPS) if you need <300ms 99th.

We can convert that to a cost estimate once we agree on target 99/95 latencies and the acceptable fallback behavior (e.g., degrade model size or return partial streaming results).

A few clarifying questions for sizing:
1) For cart summarization (the longer prompts), is your 300ms 99th target strict or relaxed? If strict, we’ll need higher concurrency or a quantized-serving profile.
2) For the streaming recommender, do you expect many concurrent streams per session (e.g., multiple tabs) or strictly one stream/session?

I’ll draft a short runbook (warm/cold capacity options + autoscale tweaks) — looping Laura to add notes on rollout and canary thresholds.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Ava Retail discovery — throughput shape & SLO asks

Alyssa — thanks, and noted. Short answers while we assemble a formal doc:

- Data retention: Redwood supports configurable retention per-environment. Standard hosted logs retained 90 days by default; we can offer 30/90/365-day options and enterprise retention via Private deployment. Logs and audit trails can be routed to your S3 or a customer-managed GCS bucket (we support KMS for encryption at rest).
- SLA during crests: our Dedicated tier can commit to availability and latency SLOs; for hosted pilots we recommend a performance validation week and a Canary with fallback to a smaller-model variant. We will provide draft SLA language and proposed credit schedule in the next 48 hours.
- Pilot timeline (30 days, rough): Week 0–1: onboarding + dataset ingest; Week 2: perf runs & telemetry capture; Week 3: crests + validation; Week 4: finalize tuning & handback notes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to produce the sizing + runbook (warm standby vs blown-up dedicated sizing) + cost back-of-envelope.
2) I’ll send a 1-page data retention + SLA summary for procurement to attach.
3) Priya/Gabe confirm whether the main crest is predictable for the daily 11:00 drop (we can pre-warm for scheduled drops).

Marissa / Laura — can you have items (1) and (2) to us by EOD Thu so procurement can proceed?

—Karthik
